definitions.explanation: Used to express relief that something turned out well.
A state of being lucky or blessed.

examples.japanese: {幸|さいわ}い、{怪我|けが}はなかった。
{幸|さいわ}いなことに、{雨|あめ}は{降|ふ}らなかった。
ご{多幸|たこう}をお{祈|いの}りします。
examples.notes: [Note: {多幸|たこう} is a formal word for happiness]

examples.japanese: {幸|さいわ}い、{電車|でんしゃ}の{遅延|ちえん}は{軽微|けいび}で、{会議|かいぎ}には{間|ま}に{合|あ}った。
examples.english: Fortunately, the train delay was minor, and I made it to the meeting on time.

notes:
{幸|さいわ}い is used to express fortune or luck.

AS ADVERB:
- {幸|さいわ}い (fortunately)
- {幸|さいわ}いなことに (fortunately)
- {幸|さいわ}いにも (luckily)

AS NOUN:
- {幸|さいわ}いを{祈|いの}る (to wish someone happiness)
- {不幸|ふこう}中の{幸|さいわ}い (a blessing in disguise)

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- {幸|さいわ}い: fortunately (neutral to formal)
- {幸運|こううん}にも: luckily (emphasizes luck)
- ありがたいことに: thankfully

FORMAL/WRITTEN:
- {幸甚|こうじん}です (I would be most grateful - very formal)
